root_cause.text: A use-after-free was caused in XFS scrub's xchk_btree_check_block_owner() by dereferencing bs->cur->bc_ops to identify bno/rmap cursor type after self-xref code could free the aliased sc->sa.{bno_cur,rmap_cur} cursor that bs->cur pointed to, due to broken temporal ordering introduced by removing xfs_btnum_t.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states “We cannot dereference bs->cur when trying to determine if bs->cur aliases bs->sc->sa.{bno,rmap}_cur after the latter has been freed” and the patch fixes this by caching xfs_btree_is_bno(bs->cur->bc_ops) and xfs_btree_is_rmap(bs->cur->bc_ops) into is_bnobt/is_rmapbt before calls like xchk_xref_is_only_owned_by() that may free those cursors, then using the cached booleans instead of dereferencing bs->cur afterward.

intent_record.intent_summary: Precompute bnobt and rmapbt cursor-type flags in xchk_btree_check_block_owner for later ownership-check logic.
intent_record.what: Two new boolean local variables, is_bnobt and is_rmapbt, were added to xchk_btree_check_block_owner, and after the existing early return for a null bs->cur, they are initialized by calling xfs_btree_is_bno(bs->cur->bc_ops) and xfs_btree_is_rmap(bs->cur->bc_ops) before computing agno and agbno.
intent_record.how: At runtime this caches whether the current btree cursor refers to a bnobt or rmapbt in local flags for later use in the function, enabling subsequent logic to make ownership checks based on btree type without repeatedly querying bc_ops; the shown hunk itself does not change control flow beyond introducing these computed values.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use cached btree-type flags instead of bs->cur dereferences when nulling the cursor to avoid invalid access during block owner cross-reference checks.
intent_record.what: The change replaces two direct type checks on bs->cur->bc_ops using xfs_btree_is_bno(...) and xfs_btree_is_rmap(...) with checks against the precomputed boolean variables is_bnobt and is_rmapbt in the conditions that set bs->cur = NULL when the corresponding scrub cursor is unavailable.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this avoids dereferencing bs->cur to inspect bc_ops in these conditional paths and instead uses previously determined btree-type state, preserving the logic that disables further owner checks when the related cursor is missing while preventing failures if bs->cur has been or could be NULL.

Author: Christoph Hellwig <hch@lst.de>
Date:   Thu Feb 22 12:40:51 2024 -0800

    xfs: remove xfs_btnum_t
    
    The last checks for bc_btnum can be replaced with helpers that check
    the btree ops.  This allows adding new btrees to XFS without having
    to update a global enum.
    
    Signed-off-by: Christoph Hellwig <hch@lst.de>
    Reviewed-by: Darrick J. Wong <djwong@kernel.org>
    [djwong: complete the ops predicates]
    Signed-off-b
bic_trace_step.reason: The diff shows the relevant logic in xchk_btree_check_block_owner clearly enough to decide. Before the self-xref calls, the code no longer saves the btree type in a stable local variable; the line `btnum = bs->cur->bc_btnum;` was removed. Instead, after `xchk_xref_is_not_shared(bs->sc, agbno, 1, bs->oinfo);` and `xchk_xref_is_only_owned_by(bs->sc, agbno, 1, bs->oinfo);`, it checks cursor type via `xfs_btree_is_bno(bs->cur->bc_ops)` and `xfs_btree_is_rmap(bs->cur->bc_ops)`. The root cause says self-xref code can free the aliased scrub cursor that `bs->cur` points to, so dereferencing `bs->cur->bc_ops` after those calls is the vulnerable use-after-free pattern. Specifically, the vulnerable constructs are `if (!bs->sc->sa.bno_cur && xfs_btree_is_bno(bs->cur->bc_ops))` and later `if (!bs->sc->sa.rmap_cur && xfs_btree_is_rmap(bs->cur->bc_ops))`, because they dereference `bs->cur` after operations that may have freed the aliased cursor. The fix is not present here because there is no stable pre-xref capture of the cursor type and no avoidance of post-xref dereference of `bs->cur->bc_ops`.

diff --git a/fs/xfs/scrub/btree.c b/fs/xfs/scrub/btree.c
bic_trace_step.reason: The function body is sufficient because it directly shows the handling around the self-xref call that can affect aliased cursors. The root cause describes a UAF from dereferencing `bs->cur->bc_ops` after self-xref code could free an aliased cursor. In this commit, the function saves the cursor type before the xref call: `btnum = bs->cur->bc_btnum;`. Then it performs the self-xref: `xfs_scrub_xref_is_used_space(bs->sc, agbno, 1);`. After that, it does not dereference `bs->cur->bc_ops`; instead it uses the saved `btnum` and checks whether the aliased bnobt cursor was cleared: `if (!bs->sc->sa.bno_cur && btnum == XFS_BTNUM_BNO) bs->cur = NULL;`. The comment explicitly acknowledges aliasing: `The bnobt scrubber aliases bs->cur to bs->sc->sa.bno_cur`. Because the function stores the cursor identity before the potentially freeing self-xref and uses the saved value afterward, the vulnerable construct described in the root cause is absent here, and the protective handling is present.
